displayName: Acme user-branch service (UniBasic → Java 21 / Spring Boot 3, feasibility POC)
description: Feasibility POC for a prospective client engagement: an equipment-finance ILS system, business logic in Rocket UniData/UniBasic, target Java 17+/PostgreSQL. Translates two REAL, public UniBasic routines (github.com/zelenko/pick — no repo-level LICENSE stated, used here read-and-analyze/attributed, not redistributed as original work) from a signed unibasic spec (targetStack=java-spring): add-branch-to-user.pick's CONVERT VM TO @FM / LOCATE / INSERT / CONVERT @FM TO VM round-trip collapses to a plain List<String>.contains/add once the field lives in a real collection (DynamicArrayOps); the OPEN 'INITIALS' TO USER + numbered READV/WRITEV,ID,9 access becomes an injected UserBranchRecordPort, with field 9's unresolved DICT name explicitly flagged rather than invented (UserBranchRecordPort, UserBranchService). Builds OFFLINE through the maven-sidecar (pinned plugins + junit/assertj only). UniData/UniVerse have no free/scriptable runtime, so source-execution equivalence is NOT claimed — the golden score + this compiling, passing JUnit suite are the gates, the same honest posture as the OpenEdge ABL archetype.

matches.fallback: Used for unibasic routines centered on multivalue field manipulation (LOCATE/INSERT/CONVERT/angle-bracket access) against a hashed-file record.
